docs.purpose: Every night this job rebuilds the pre-computed monthly permit summary that the admin dashboard reads, so the numbers shown there reflect the permits loaded earlier that day. It runs after the nightly permit-loading window so it never summarises a half-finished import. It rebuilds the summary in the background, so the dashboard stays readable the whole time it is working.
docs.data_story: It reads `permits` and writes `mv_monthly_permit_stats`. It runs on `30 14 * * *`, unattended, with nobody watching — which is why its guard matters: pg_extension guard with a NOTICE-skip, measured (migrations/233:78-81 — `IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'pg_cron')` then RAISE NOTICE and RETURN); plus an idempotent unschedule-by-name loop over cron.job before scheduling.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **JOB descriptor** of archetype `SCHEDULED` under its own `job.schema.json` (Spec 128 R-14) — declaring its schedule, its target, its idempotency posture, its behaviour when `pg_cron` is absent, and the audit row it writes. Nothing about how it runs changes; what changes is that those five answers stop living only in SQL and YAML.

contracts: none — a pg_cron job takes no request and calls no API route

versioning.why: CONCURRENTLY depends on the matview keeping its unique index (month, permit_type); changing the matview shape breaks the refresh, and migration 034 is pinned by a source-scan test.

inputs.why: It re-reads the permits table — a pipeline-written table — through the matview definition; there is no contract and no parameter.

outputs.why: NOT ANSWERABLE from the closed set: outputs offers none | contract_only | optimistic_then_contract | device_only, all of which describe a client writing through an API. This job writes directly to the database with no contract in between. The substance is recorded in outputs.tables[]; the vocabulary gap is a Spec 128 §4 escalation (R-14: JOBs need job.schema.json). What it does: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY public.mv_monthly_permit_stats — it rewrites the matview and touches no base table.

tables.chain_position: n/a — a pg_cron job, not a chain step

state.why: The matview IS the state, and it is entirely server-side; the job holds nothing across runs.

staleness.why: It is the thing that defines another surface's freshness: the market-metrics query reads the matview, so that page is exactly as fresh as this job's last nightly run.

session.why: NOT ANSWERABLE from the closed set: guards.session offers anon | authenticated | entitled | admin, all of which describe an end-user principal. This runs with no request and no user — as the pg_cron job owner through a SECURITY DEFINER function, or as a GitHub Actions runner holding repository secrets. Spec 128 §4 escalation (Spec 128 R-14 already anticipates JOBs getting their own job.schema.json); recorded rather than mis-answered.

rls_class.why: permits and the matview are both pipeline-owned — not Class A and not profiles, so Class B by the catalog's default rule: RLS on, zero policies, service-role only.

checks.why: REFRESH ... CONCURRENTLY requires the matview to carry a unique index; idx_mv_monthly_month_type (month, permit_type) is that index and Spec 115 §5 records it as live-verified. Drop it and the nightly refresh starts erroring instead of degrading.
It writes no pipeline_runs row, so the freshness of the matview the market-metrics dashboard reads cannot be observed from the house observability surface — only from the matview contents themselves.

14:30 UTC was chosen to land after the 11:00 UTC coa->permits window plus its ~3h worst case; if that window moves, this slot has to move with it, and the previous 09:30 slot was wrong for exactly this reason.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM public.mv_monthly_permit_stats WHERE month > (CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '1 month')
plausibility.why: The matview groups by date_trunc of issued_date; a month beyond next month means a permit carries a future issue date, which is a source-data problem this aggregate would otherwise hide.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM public.mv_monthly_permit_stats WHERE total_value < 0
plausibility.why: total_value is COALESCE(SUM(est_const_cost), 0); a negative total can only come from negative cost rows, which are not a legitimate value.

errors.why: No exception handling: the scheduled command is the bare REFRESH statement, so a failure leaves yesterday's snapshot in place and a cron.job_run_details row nobody reads.

emits.why: No pipeline_runs row and no audit row — the refresh is silent whether it succeeds or fails.

offers.why: A matview refresh renders no sponsored placement.

config.why: No tunable at all — the schedule is a literal cron expression in the migration and the matview definition is fixed in 034.

sharing.why: It renders no contract; the matview it maintains is read by src/lib/market-metrics/queries.ts, which is a consumer of its output, not a shared contract of this job.

limitations.what: The matview has no freshness signal of its own.
limitations.measured: migrations/233_pg_cron_maintenance_catalog.sql:89-93 — the scheduled command is one REFRESH statement with no pipeline_runs insert; nothing on src/lib/market-metrics/queries.ts:83 can tell how old the aggregate is.

limitations.what: It was net-new when scheduled — nothing refreshed this matview for the years between 034 and 233.
limitations.measured: docs/specs/00-architecture/115_scheduling.md §5 records it as "Net-new — no automated refresh exists in the codebase today (034 created it; nothing schedules its refresh)".

notes: Command is `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY public.mv_monthly_permit_stats`; the reads_tables entry `permits` is measured from the matview definition at migrations/034_mv_monthly_permit_stats.sql:14. CONCURRENTLY is legal because of the unique index idx_mv_monthly_month_type. MEASURED 2026-09-15. The consumer is src/lib/market-metrics/queries.ts:83 (reached by the admin market-metrics route) — that is the surface whose staleness this job defines, and it has no way to see when the refresh last ran. The matview definition is migrations/034_mv_monthly_permit_stats.sql:8-16, introspected into src/lib/db/generated/schema.ts:2323, so the four columns above are read from the live database rather than typed from the migration. guards.session and outputs.answer are Spec 128 §4 vocabulary escalations, not unmeasured facts; render.targets keeps ["screen"] only because the schema requires one of screen|pdf|csv|email and a job renders none.
